page: PDF 155 / printed 135; PDF 161 / printed 141; PDF 169 / printed 149; PDF 175 / printed 155
issue: Four of the five figure captions in this batch contain duplicated or garbled clauses - the same sentence fragment appears twice, or a clause is left half-finished. This is one systematic caption-assembly defect, not four independent typos, and it is visible to every reader. Examples as rendered: FIG 7.8 "... the 24.9 GB KV budget of 17.5 -> 17 concurrent (floor 17, not 18: ..." repeated; FIG 8.1 "compute, memory and interconnect are separate bandwidths are distinct architectural constraints" repeated and ungrammatical; FIG 8.2 "a kernel's position on the roofline is a theoretical bound on the roofline - it is not a measured latency" and "host-level attainable performance additional depends on sharding and communication"; FIG 8.3 "For aligned F=4k+1, F_I2V=1+4x(31-1) = 121 latent time positions correspond to frame" and the repeated "not autoregressive text decode" point. FIG 7.7's caption is clean, which is presumably why the defect survived earlier rounds.
evidence: Captions on PDF p.155 / printed p.135 (FIG 7.8), PDF p.161 / printed p.141 (FIG 8.1), PDF p.169 / printed p.149 (FIG 8.2), PDF p.175 / printed p.155 (FIG 8.3). FIG 7.7 (PDF p.154) is clean.
acceptance_test: A duplicate-phrase scan over every figure caption in the book returns zero hits; each caption reads as one clean argument with no repeated clause and no unfinished clause; the four captions above are re-read aloud by a second person before release.

issue: The caption's index notation is internally inconsistent and cannot be checked against the figure. 'r' is defined as a rank index (r = 0...N-1) and then reused as a round index (r = 0...N-2) in the same sentence; 's' is introduced ('indexed reduce-scatter rounds') and never used again; 't' is introduced for all-gather rounds and then not used (the caption switches back to 'r'); 'i' (chunk index) is never defined. The clause 'rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N and retains chunk i' is also not satisfiable: because rank r sends chunk r in round 0, it accumulates chunks (r-1), (r-2), (r-3) and retains chunk (r+1) mod N, not chunk i.
evidence: Caption as printed: 'Indices are per phase: r = 0...N-1, s = indexed reduce-scatter rounds; t = 0...N-1 all-gather rounds; r = 0...N-2 rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N and retains chunk i; in round r of the all-gather (r = 0...N-2) rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N, beginning with its own reduced chunk i.' The figure carries no chunk indices, no round labels and no rank-to-chunk mapping, so none of the caption's index claims is verifiable from the drawing. The all-gather clause is the one correct piece (rank r holds chunk i_r and sends (i_r - t) mod N); the reduce-scatter clause is not.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the index clause with one symbol per role (e.g. q = rank, t = round, j = chunk), state the ring direction explicitly, and either delete 's' and 't' or use them consistently. Acceptance: every symbol is defined exactly once and used; the reduce-scatter and all-gather rules are each checkable against the drawn boxes; and the 'retains chunk' clause matches the drawn rank-to-chunk assignment (see FIG-9.2-01).

issue: The two ring-time displays on printed p.168 do not evaluate to their stated results as rendered, and the symbolic form appears to be missing a factor in each case, so the reader cannot reproduce Figure 9.1's plotted points from the book's own model. Escalate to P1 if the source matches the render. The correct ring all-reduce model is T = 2*(N-1)/N * M / B_eff.
evidence: As rendered at 150 dpi, display 1 reads T_ring ~ (N-1)/N * M / B_eff ~ ... GB / 8.40 GB/s ~ 6.1 s. (N-1)/N * M = 122.5 GB; 122.5/8.40 = 14.6 s, not 6.1 s. The stated 6.1 s equals 245 GB / 40 GB/s = 2*(7/8)*140 GB / 40 GB/s, which is exactly Figure 9.1's HDR point (6,125 ms) - so the symbolic numerator is missing the leading factor 2. Display 2 reads T_ring ~ 2*140 GB / 8 * 2.5 GB/s ~ 98 s; (2*140/8)/2.5 = 14 s and (2*140/8)*2.5 = 87.5 s, neither of which is 98 s; 98 s requires 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s, i.e. the numerator is missing the (N-1) factor (98 = 7 x 14). The prose's ratios ('about 11x the ideal NVLink ring time', 'about 180x') are consistent with 6.1 s and 98 s against Fig 9.1's 544 ms, so the results are right and the displayed algebra is what is suspect. NOT VERIFIED against source: the 150-dpi render is ambiguous for the substituted numerals and for a possible leading '2 *' in display 1.
acceptance_test: Confirm the source text of both displays before editing. Acceptance: each display's symbolic form and its substituted numerals evaluate to the printed result (6.1 s and 98 s) and to the corresponding points in Figure 9.1 (245 GB sent per rank / B_eff); the symbolic form explicitly carries the factor 2 for the two phases and the (N-1)/N factor; and the substituted numerator is legible at print size as 245 GB (or 2*(7/8)*140 GB).

issue: The prose says the multi-rail effective bandwidth is 'referenced in Section 9.2 and Fig 9.1', but the value used (8.40 GB/s) appears in neither location.
evidence: Printed p.168: 'the multi-rail effective bandwidth referenced in Section 9.2 and Fig 9.1'. Section 9.2 (printed p.162) quotes 900/450 GB/s NVLink, 25 GB/s nominal HDR and 2.5 GB/s effective Ethernet; Figure 9.1's three curves are 450, 40 and 2.5 GB/s. 8.40 GB/s occurs in neither.
acceptance_test: Either cite the location where 8.40 GB/s is established, or reword to reference the concept rather than a value. Acceptance: every numeric value in the sentence can be located in the cited section or figure.

issue: The blue NVLink curve is clipped by the 0.1 ms axis floor at the left of the plot, so the drawn line appears to originate at 0.1 ms rather than at its model value, inviting the reader to read a floor value that the model does not produce.
evidence: Model t = 1.75*x/B. At x = 0.01 GB, t = 0.0175/450 s = 0.039 ms, below the plotted floor of 0.1 ms; the curve enters the axes at x ~ 0.026 GB. The rendered line appears to start at the bottom-left corner at 0.1 ms. The orange (0.44 ms) and red (7 ms) curves are inside the axes at x = 0.01, so only the blue curve is affected.
acceptance_test: Either extend the y-axis floor to ~0.01 ms, or annotate the clipped region, or start the x-axis where all three curves are inside the axes. Acceptance: no drawn curve endpoint coincides with an axis limit unless that limit is the model value.

issue: Figure 9.2 uses colour for two different meanings simultaneously - the phase labels ('Reduce-scatter' in orange, 'All-gather' in blue) and the box borders (orange = single reduced element, blue = full four-element vector) - and, unlike Figure 10.1, it carries no grayscale note.

figure: Figure 9.3 — column identification and title/structure mismatch

Separately, both the caption's MPI caveat and the figure's own note concern MPI, which appears in no box on the payload path.

The title 'The payload path is not the bootstrap path' is carried solely by the dashed red control arrows at the top, while the dominant structure is a two-column vendor comparison. issue: Panel A's communication note understates the collective traffic of tensor parallelism, and the panel does not show the replicated activations that the surrounding prose says are replicated. A reader could infer that TP replicates weights and communicates once per layer.
evidence: Panel A note: 'communication: all-reduce every layer -> on-node in the canonical config (NVLink)'. In a standard transformer block with column/row-parallel projections, TP requires an all-reduce (or reduce-scatter + all-gather) at each row-parallel projection output - typically two per block (attention output projection and MLP down-projection) - plus an all-gather for the column-parallel input, so 'every layer' understates the per-block collective count by roughly 2x. The prose below the figure states 'activations are replicated', but Panel A draws only the weight bar and the all-reduce arrow, so nothing in the panel shows what is replicated. This matters because the book's own communication arithmetic elsewhere (e.g. the ring model on printed p.168) is sensitive to the number of collectives per block.
acceptance_test: Revise the note to state the collective count per transformer block (e.g. 'all-reduce at each row-parallel projection - typically two per transformer block') and add a replicated-activation element to Panel A or name it in the panel text. Acceptance: the panel's communication note matches the collective count used elsewhere in the book, and the panel shows or names what is replicated.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 — P/D disaggregation has two cases, two different KV links
issue: The headline transfer labels ('35 GB ≈ 0.08 s (on-node, unidirectional)' and '35 GB ≈ 0.9 s (cross-host)') do not carry the assumption that the arithmetic depends on, namely that the whole 35 GB crosses ONE unsharded link. The figure's own caveat supplies it ('conservative; shard = 0.02 s'), but the caveat is small print at the bottom of the figure while the headline numbers are the visually dominant text. A reader who reads only the labels will conclude that on-node KV migration costs 0.08 s, when the figure's own drawing (4 prefill GPUs -> 4 decode GPUs) admits a 4-way sharded transfer at 0.02 s.
evidence: Printed p. 196 (PDF 216) states the same assumption explicitly: 'That is the whole 35 GB over one unsharded link — a conservative bound; the panel's 4-way shard would be 35 / (4 x 450) = 0.02 s.' The figure's Case A arrow is labeled '450 GB/s per GPU' while the time is computed as 35 GB / 450 GB/s (one link), so the label and the arithmetic use different bandwidths unless the unsharded assumption is stated at the label.
acceptance_test: Move the assumption into the headline labels, e.g. '35 GB over one unsharded 450 GB/s link ≈ 0.08 s (4-way shard: 0.02 s)', or add a one-line note directly under the Case A arrow. Acceptance: the 0.08 s figure cannot be read without the unsharded-link condition being visible at the same scale as the number.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 — P/D disaggregation has two cases, two different KV links
issue: The caveat's parenthetical '(per-GPU in a per-host NIC)' conflates the two link types the figure is built to contrast: Case A's link is NVLink, per-GPU (450 GB/s per direction); Case B's link is a host NIC, per-host (40 GB/s). As written, the parenthetical reads as if 'per-GPU' and 'per-host NIC' describe the same link, which is precisely the distinction the figure exists to make.
evidence: Rendered caveat text: 'Per-request times assume an unsharded dedicated link (per-GPU in a per-host NIC); 1.4 TB/s exceeds any single link above.' The two cases are labeled '450 GB/s per GPU' (NVLink) and '40 GB/s per host' (NIC) respectively, so the parenthetical should name one link per case.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as two clauses, e.g. 'Case A assumes one unsharded NVLink direction per GPU (450 GB/s); Case B assumes one dedicated host NIC (40 GB/s).' Acceptance: each parenthetical maps unambiguously to exactly one of the two cases.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 — P/D disaggregation has two cases, two different KV links
issue: The caveat's first clause appears to read 'A: 0.08 s x whole 35 GB over one unsharded 450 GB/s link', using a multiplication sign where the relation is equality (35 GB / 450 GB/s = 0.08 s). If the glyph is a multiplication sign, the sentence is not a valid statement; if it is an equals sign, the clause is fine but reads awkwardly.
evidence: Rendered caveat line: 'A: 0.08 s x whole 35 GB over one unsharded 450 GB/s link (conservative; shard = 0.02 s).' The same figure elsewhere uses '=' correctly ('35 GB/request x 40 req/s = 1.4 TB/s of payload'), so the operator set is inconsistent within one block.
acceptance_test: Inspect the source glyph. If it is a multiplication sign, replace with '=' (or rewrite as 'A: 0.08 s = 35 GB over one unsharded 450 GB/s link'). Acceptance: the caveat contains no operator that misstates the relation between 0.08 s, 35 GB, and 450 GB/s.

figure: FIGURE 11.3 — P/D disaggregation has two cases, two different KV links
issue: The label 'illustrative 13.3K-token, FP16 full-MHA' does not say WHICH tokens cross the link. In P/D disaggregation the KV that moves is the prefill-produced KV (the prompt), not the full sequence including generated tokens; the figure's own flow row ('prompt -> generated tokens -> prompt -> generated tokens ->') implies prompt-only KV, but the label is silent. A reader who takes 13.3K as the total sequence length would overstate the transferred KV by the output length.
evidence: Printed p. 196 (PDF 216) resolves it in prose — '13.3K prefill would be ~1.86 PFLOP' — confirming 13.3K is the prefill/prompt length. The figure and its caption do not carry that qualifier, so the figure is not self-contained.
acceptance_test: Change the label to 'illustrative 13.3K-token prompt (prefill KV), FP16 full-MHA' in both panels, or add 'prompt tokens only' to the caption's first sentence. Acceptance: the figure alone makes clear that the transferred KV covers the prompt, not the generated tokens.

figure: FIGURE 11.1 — Discrete vs continuous batching (Orca-style slot diagram)
issue: The caption declares a single horizontal axis ('The horizontal axis is time (decode steps / iterations)'), but the two panels are drawn on different scales and different x-origins: the discrete panel's batch spans roughly x=95..250 px while the continuous panel's rows span roughly x=310..410 px. The axis label appears only under the left panel. A reader comparing durations across the panels — the natural comparison for a 'discrete vs continuous' figure — will be misled, because equal pixel distances do not represent equal numbers of decode steps.
evidence: Rendered page: the 'time -> decode steps / iterations ->' label sits under the discrete panel only; the continuous panel has no axis and no gridlines; the two panels' horizontal extents differ by roughly a factor of two.
acceptance_test: Either align both panels to a shared time grid with a single axis spanning both, or add to the caption 'the two panels are drawn at different horizontal scales and are not directly comparable in duration.' Acceptance: the figure cannot be read as supporting a cross-panel duration comparison unless the panels are on a common scale.
